'''Esteban Félix Granero Molina''' ({{IPA|es|esˈteβaɱ ˈfeliɣs ɣɾaˈneɾo moˈlina}}; born 2 July 1987) is a Spanish former professional [[Association football|footballer]]. Known as ''El Pirata'' ("The Pirate"),<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2011/09/15/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1316065301.html|title=#Granero, el Pirata bohemio|trans-title=#Granero, the bohemian pirate|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|first=Nacho|last=Labarga|language=es|date=15 September 2011|access-date=6 September 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/mercado-fichajes/el-pirata-granero-huye-de-madrid-para-ser-el-lider-del-qpr-2193987|title='El Pirata' Granero huye de Madrid para ser el líder del QPR|trans-title='The Pirate' Granero runs from Madrid to be QPR leader|newspaper=[[Sport (Spanish newspaper)|Sport]]|first=Alejandro|last=Alcázar|language=es|date=30 August 2012|access-date=19 October 2019}}</ref> he could play as a [[Midfielder#Central midfielder|central]] or an [[Midfielder#Attacking midfielder|attacking midfielder]].

He emerged through [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]'s youth academy, but made a name for himself in [[La Liga]] with [[Getafe CF|Getafe]], following which he returned to his previous club, winning three major titles but being sparingly played over the course of three seasons. In the Spanish top division he also represented [[Real Sociedad]] and [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]], achieving totals of 264 games and 18 goals.

Granero represented [[Spain national football team|Spain]] at [[Spain national under-21 football team|under-21 level]], appearing in the [[2009 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|2009 European Championship]].

==Club career==
===Real Madrid===
Born in [[Madrid]],<ref name=Past/> Granero joined ranks of [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] when he was just eight years old, and quickly began displaying his footballing talent. In one season, he scored 83 goals in the under-10 division and, in 1999, [[Captain (association football)|captained]] the under-12 side that won the International Football-7 tournament held at the [[Palau Sant Jordi]] in [[Barcelona]] by defeating [[FC Barcelona (youth)|FC Barcelona]] 1–0 with his [[Overtime (sports)|extra time]] goal – he was also named the best player of the competition.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2005/11/29/mas_futbol/1133249260_850215.html|title=Es todo un honor que me comparen con Zidane|trans-title=I am really honoured to be compared to Zidane|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Rubén|last=Cañizares|language=es|date=29 November 2005|access-date=28 November 2017}}</ref>

Granero, alongside teammates [[Juan Mata]] and [[Alberto Bueno]], won the ''[[Copa de Campeones Juvenil de Fútbol]]'' in 2006,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.terra.es/deportes/articulo/html/dpo209974.htm|title=1–0 El Madrid gana torneo ante un Valladolid que no estuvo cómodo|trans-title=1–0 Madrid win tournament against uncomfortable Valladolid|publisher=[[Terra (company)|Terra]]|language=es|date=7 May 2006|access-date=9 November 2008}}</ref> an under-19 official youth tournament organized by the [[Royal Spanish Football Federation]]. He then joined the club's [[Real Madrid C|C team]] at the age of 17, standing out for his talent and passing skills and going on to receive the ''Números 1 Don Balón'' award as the "Most Valuable Player" of the Group VII of [[Tercera División]] in [[2005–06 Tercera División|2005–06]], an accolade bestowed by ''[[Don Balón]]'' magazine, one of the founding members of [[European Sports Media]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.qpr.co.uk/news/archive/esteban-granero-in-profile/|title=Esteban Granero – In profile|publisher=Queens Park Rangers F.C.|date=30 August 2012|access-date=15 February 2023}}</ref> That same season he made his first appearance with [[Real Madrid Castilla]] in a match against [[Albacete Balompié]], during which he had an [[Assist (association football)|assist]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://web.eldia.es/2005-11-28/jornada/jornada53.htm|title=Triunfo cómodo del Castilla|trans-title=Easy win for Castilla|newspaper=[[El Día (Canary Islands)|El Día]]|language=es|date=28 November 2005|access-date=28 November 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201031532/http://web.eldia.es/2005-11-28/jornada/jornada53.htm|archive-date=1 December 2017}}</ref>
[[Image:Granero 02 2007.jpg|thumb|left|Granero in 2007]]

===Getafe===
Granero made the definitive jump to Castilla in [[2006–07 Segunda División|2006–07]]'s [[Segunda División]], and slowly earned the confidence of coach [[Míchel (footballer, born 1963)|Míchel]] until finally becoming an undisputed starter.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vavel.com/es/futbol/2013/11/26/real-madrid/305872.html|title=La última plantilla que descendió con el Castilla. ¿Qué fue de ellos?|trans-title=The last squad to be relegated with Castilla. What happened to them?|publisher=Vavel|first=Miguel Ángel|last=Balderas|language=es|date=26 November 2013|access-date=20 January 2020}}</ref> He would eventually fail to make the transition into the first team, as did fellow ''[[cantera]]'' players [[Rubén de la Red]], [[Javi García]] and [[Adrián González (footballer, born 1988)|Adrián González]] and, on 31 August, the last day of the transfer window, he moved to [[Getafe CF]] (also in Madrid) on a one-year loan; de la Red moved in the same direction, albeit in a different deal.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archivo.marca.com/edicion/marca/futbol/1a_division/getafe/es/desarrollo/1031072.html|title=De la Red y Granero fichan por el Getafe|trans-title=De la Red and Granero sign for Getafe|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=31 August 2007|access-date=29 January 2018}}</ref>

After [[2007–08 La Liga|the season]]'s end, in which both he and de la Red were instrumental in the team's campaign that included runs to the [[2007–08 UEFA Cup|quarter-finals]] in the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] and [[2007–08 Copa del Rey|the final]] of the [[Copa del Rey]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.20minutos.es/deportes/noticia/valencia-copa-getafe-370181/0/|title=Un perdón con forma de Copa (3–1)|trans-title=Pardon in the shape of a Cup (3–1)|newspaper=[[20 minutos]]|language=es|date=17 April 2008|access-date=29 January 2018}}</ref> Granero returned to Real Madrid. However, on 13 July 2008, he joined Getafe permanently, with Real keeping a re-buy option on the player.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/01cf-0f84e103d9f3-6b7859878e7e-1000--getafe-get-their-man-in-granero/|title=Getafe get their man in Granero|publisher=UEFA|date=14 July 2008|access-date=10 June 2010}}</ref>

===Return to Real===
On 21 July 2009, Real Madrid exercised their buyback option in a reported [[Euro|€]]4 million deal,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11841_5449305,00.html|title=Granero returns to Real|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|first=Chris|last=Burton|date=23 July 2009|access-date=29 July 2009}}</ref> and Granero scored three goals during preseason. His first official one came in his first start, when he opened a 3–0 [[La Liga]] away win over [[RCD Espanyol]] on 12 September.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=275781&cc=4716|title=Madrid maintain perfect start|publisher=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|date=12 September 2009|access-date=12 September 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121102085334/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=275781&cc=4716|archive-date=2 November 2012}}</ref> In his [[2009–10 La Liga|first season]], where his team eventually came out empty in silverware, he alternated [[Substitute (association football)|the bench]] with starts, with irregular performances.
 
In the [[2010–11 La Liga|2010–11 campaign]], after the club purchased two players in similar positions, [[Sami Khedira]] and [[Mesut Özil]], Granero was limited mainly to substitute appearances. On 16 January 2011 he scored as a substitute against [[UD Almería]], in a 1–1 draw at the bottom-placed side.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/301973?cc=5739|title=Real held by lowly Almeria|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=16 January 2011|access-date=17 January 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110119021701/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/301973?cc=5739|archive-date=19 January 2011}}</ref>

Granero's situation became worse in [[2011–12 La Liga|2011–12]], with even [[Fábio Coentrão]] – another compatriot of manager [[José Mourinho]] who was signed in the off-season, originally as a left full-back – being preferred over him as central midfielder.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2011/09/02/mas_futbol/1314944835_850215.html|title=De la energía de Coentrao, al pase de Granero o el trivote|trans-title=From Coentrão's energy, to Granero's pass or holding midfield trio|newspaper=Diario AS|language=es|date=2 September 2011|access-date=15 February 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://espanol.eurosport.com/futbol/la-liga/2011-2012/granero-pudo-irse-al-betis_sto3128631/story.shtml|title=Granero pudo irse al Betis|trans-title=Granero could have gone to Betis|publisher=Eurosport|language=es|date=27 January 2012|access-date=15 February 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ondacero.es/hemeroteca/coentrao-diez-mas_201203285542806e0cf2c2fca209a7ec.html|title=Coentrao y diez más|trans-title=Coentrão and ten more|publisher=[[Onda Cero]]|language=es|date=28 March 2012|access-date=15 February 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.defensacentral.com/real_madrid/72660-primer-equipo-imprescindible-pocos-minutos-conceder-pocas-oportunidades-esteban-granero-manter-plantilla/|title=Granero, un imprescindible con pocos minutos|trans-title=Granero, untouchable with few minutes|publisher=Defensa Central|first=Jaime|last=De Carlos|language=es|date=9 July 2012|access-date=24 July 2012}}</ref>

===Queens Park Rangers===
On 30 August 2012, Granero signed a four-year contract with English club [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] after transferring for a reported fee of [[Pound sterling|£]]9 million, and was handed the number 14 shirt.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.qpr.co.uk/news/article/300812-granero-signs-343656.aspx|title=Exclusive: Granero completes move|publisher=Queens Park Rangers F.C.|date=30 August 2012|access-date=30 August 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/2896/premier-league/2012/08/30/3342344/official-granero-joins-qpr-on-four-year-deal?source=breakingnews|title=Official: Granero joins QPR on four-year deal|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|first=Jay|last=Jaffa|date=30 August 2012|access-date=30 August 2012}}</ref> He made his [[Premier League]] debut two days later, starting in a 3–1 away loss against defending champions [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/uk/en/report/345814/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5739|title=Manchester City 3–1 Queens Park Rangers|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=1 September 2012|access-date=6 September 2012}}</ref>

Granero scored his first goal for QPR on 6 October 2012, but in a 3–2 defeat at [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19776317|title=West Brom 3–2 QPR|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|first=John|last=Stanton|date=6 October 2012|access-date=8 October 2012}}</ref>

===Real Sociedad===
On 15 August 2013, after [[2012–13 Premier League|his team's relegation]], Granero was loaned to [[Real Sociedad]] in a [[2013–14 La Liga|season]]-long move.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.qpr.co.uk/news/article/150813-granero-sociedad-994513.aspx|title=Granero pens Sociedad loan|publisher=Queens Park Rangers|date=15 August 2013|access-date=15 August 2013}}</ref> On 17 September, after entering the pitch in the 81st minute of an eventual 0–2 home loss against [[FC Shakhtar Donetsk]] in the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League|group stage]] of the [[UEFA Champions League]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/020d-0e8629d939d0-7056a3fdede2-1000--teixeira-on-target-as-shakhtar-ruin-real-s-night/|title=Teixeira on target as Shakhtar ruin Real's night|publisher=UEFA|first=Graham|last=Hunter|date=17 September 2013|access-date=18 September 2013}}</ref> he suffered an [[anterior cruciate ligament]] injury to his right knee, being sidelined for approximately six months.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2013/09/17/futbol/equipos/real_sociedad/1379454497.html|title=Granero tiene roto el cruzado|trans-title=Granero has damaged cruciate|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=18 September 2013|access-date=18 September 2013}}</ref>

Following his loan, Granero signed a long-term deal on 28 July 2014 for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11095/9398212/premier-league-qpr-midfielder-esteban-granero-has-finalised-a-permanent-move-to-spanish-side-real-sociedad|title=Premier League: QPR midfielder Esteban Granero has finalised a permanent move to Spanish side Real Sociedad.|publisher=Sky Sports|date=28 July 2014|access-date=28 July 2014}}</ref> He played his first game in his second spell on 24 August, starting in a 1–0 away defeat to [[SD Eibar]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/spanish-primera-divisi%C3%B3n/story/2001649/eibar-beat-real-sociedad-in-la-liga|title=Lara seals dream start for Eibar|publisher=ESPN FC|date=24 August 2014|access-date=10 July 2017}}</ref>

===Espanyol===
On 7 July 2017, Granero signed a three-year contract with Espanyol.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rcdespanyol.com/en/news/granero-fourth-signing/_n:5397/|title=Granero, fourth signing!|publisher=RCD Espanyol|date=7 July 2017|access-date=13 July 2017}}</ref> He appeared in 25 matches in his [[2017–18 La Liga|first season]], adding 28 [[2018–19 La Liga|the following]].<ref name=DLG>{{cite web|url=https://www.diariolagrada.com/noticias/espanyol/granero-rescindira-hoy-contrato_33523.html|title=Granero rescindirá hoy su contrato|trans-title=Granero will terminate his contract today|publisher=Diario La Grada|language=es|date=30 January 2020|access-date=18 March 2020|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200318143619/https://www.diariolagrada.com/noticias/espanyol/granero-rescindira-hoy-contrato_33523.html|archive-date=18 March 2020}}</ref>

Granero scored his first league goal for the [[Catalonia|Catalans]] on 18 February 2018, in a 1–1 home draw against [[Villarreal CF]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2017_18/la-liga/jornada_24/esp_vil/|title=Granero cambia la realidad|trans-title=Granero changes the reality|newspaper=Marca|first=Ángel|last=Rodríguez|language=es|date=18 February 2018|access-date=18 March 2020}}</ref> On 30 January 2020, he left the [[RCDE Stadium]] by mutual consent.<ref name=DLG/>

===Marbella===
The same day he became a [[free agent]], Granero joined [[Marbella FC]] until June 2021.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.diariosur.es/deportes/marbella/marbella-ficha-granero-20200130105128-nt.html|title=El Marbella sorprende y ficha a Granero|trans-title=Marbella surprise and sign Granero|newspaper=[[Diario Sur]]|first=Borja|last=Gutiérrez|language=es|date=30 January 2020|access-date=18 March 2020}}</ref> He made his [[Segunda División B]] debut on 2 February 2020 at the age of 32 years and 7 months, playing 18 minutes in the 0–0 draw away to [[Mérida AD]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://eldesmarque.com/malaga/futbol-provincial/218492-el-marbella-no-pasa-del-empate-en-el-estreno-de-granero-0-0|title=El Marbella no pasa del empate en el estreno de Granero (0–0)|trans-title=Marbella can only draw in Granero debut (0–0)|publisher=El Desmarque|language=es|date=2 February 2020|access-date=18 March 2020|archive-date=18 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200318143727/https://eldesmarque.com/malaga/futbol-provincial/218492-el-marbella-no-pasa-del-empate-en-el-estreno-de-granero-0-0|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Granero announced his retirement on 5 July 2021.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.larazon.es/deportes/laotraliga/20210705/akwpkbp3qjfppaoz5mxky7m4sm.html|title=Esteban Granero se retira sin rencor y pidiendo perdón|trans-title=Esteban Granero retires holding no grudges and asking for forgiveness|newspaper=[[La Razón (Madrid)|La Razón]]|language=es|date=5 July 2021|access-date=5 July 2021}}</ref>

==International career==
After having helped [[Spain national under-19 football team|Spain]] to the [[2006 UEFA European Under-19 Championship]],<ref name=U19>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/ec-u19-06.html|title=European U-19 Championship 2006|publisher=[[RSSSF]]|first=Julián|last=Díaz Rubio|access-date=6 July 2018}}</ref> Granero made his debut for the [[Spain national under-21 football team|under-21s]] on 6 February 2007, in a [[Exhibition game#International football|friendly]] against [[England national under-21 football team|England]] (2–2).<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2007/feb/07/newsstory.englandfootballteam|title=Lita arrives late and does his level best for Pearce's England|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|first=Richard|last=Rae|date=7 February 2007|access-date=11 July 2017}}</ref> He appeared for the nation at the [[2009 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|2009 European Under-21 Championship]], in an eventual group stage exit.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/under21/news/0257-0de9640247b4-9391c746a885-1000--too-little-too-late-for-spain/|title=Too little too late for Spain|publisher=UEFA|first=John|last=Atkin|date=22 June 2009|access-date=6 July 2018}}</ref>
